Claude: correct the record guide's description of which code admits events and runs the fold. Queue after your existing work through #21356; keep all earlier queue positions and full Tailapp I7 intact.

The [guide](docs/concepts/record.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:64) says the newest ratified admission-profile governance statement chooses the rules a workroom runs. That describes a library selection model as an active submission switch. The [actual submitter](internal/app/app.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:2284) installs the application's allowlist and admission hooks; [admitApplication](internal/app/admission.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:316) evaluates new submissions against the verified pre-sequence world. [Interpreter selection](internal/app/host.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:93) is fixed when a workspace opens from its supported host binding.

I reproduced the distinction through the real Act/AcceptSubmission path in a disposable test workroom: a ratified governance record named an unavailable contract, the library resolver selected it, and the next assertion still appended effectively under the unchanged installed interpreter. [Probe evidence](admission-profile-probe.json) and [probe source](admission-profile-probe_test.go) are attached. This is a documentation mismatch, not an admitted-security-exploit claim. Historical #739 commissioned the governance/selection library; the [deployment note](notes/2026-08-07-deployment.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:1537) explicitly distinguishes it from downstream machinery that remains unimplemented. Do not reopen #739 or implement a new admission-profile runtime to make the prose true.

Deliver a small documentation correction in request/record-guide-admission-clarity:

1. Replace the misleading admission paragraph with a concise account of the shipped boundaries: installed application guards govern submission; admission-profile records and their library selector do not replace those guards or load a bundle. Distinguish host binding/interpreter availability from workroom governance records. Explain only what a reader needs, linking maintained architecture detail where useful.
2. In the adjacent fold paragraph, distinguish the deterministic fold library from the resident and CLI that actually invoke it. Remove the blanket claim that gitseq never runs a fold on the reader's behalf. Preserve independent replay and recorded-versus-effective acts.
3. Rest the corrected page on current implementation artifacts for the behavior it describes. Reconcile each cited owner and the current host-binding contract; preserve ordinary staleness honestly. The attached current-basis check selects incorporated revisions whose relevant file bytes match examined main. Do not retire unrelated wider or foreign candidates.
4. Verify the exact prose against source and the attached behavioral counterexample. Use existing focused host-binding/admission tests plus the documented documentation gates, links and owning-head file previews. A new permanent wording-only test is unnecessary. If retaining a behavioral regression, make it prove the boundary rather than repeat a sentence. Obtain independent Architecture/Security/Simplification review, ratify it, seal the approved head to main with exact-path succession, push, check required CI and remove the owned branch/worktree.

Scope is docs/concepts/record.md and only a directly necessary supporting reference correction found during this check. No runtime, governance-kind, authority, schema, dependency, public API, reader deployment, historical cleanup or broad documentation rewrite. This repairs current prose discovered during the #3029 migration audit; it does not declare every original migration condition complete. #21309 separately owns the event-ID page update and its source-basis finding already sent in chat.

body.conditions: Correct the record guide admission-profile and fold-execution claims to match shipped application/host behavior; reconcile behavior bases; verify focused evidence and documentation; independently review, seal/push main, verify CI and clean up. No runtime or governance change.
body.head: 3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b

Claude: remove contradictory promise-only completion guidance from the two reference pages below. Queue after #21365 and preserve your existing queue and active I7/review work. This is a documentation correction to shipped behavior.

At exact main 3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b, the [gs state report-basis paragraph](docs/reference/gs/state.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:267) says every report requires an effective promise, while the next paragraph permits reporting against the request. Its adjacent artifact paragraph also describes only the promised shape. The [MCP ratify authority paragraph](docs/reference/mcp/ratify.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:57) describes the originating request only through a promise. A reader trying to finish already-done work can infer that they must manufacture a promise before reporting.

The [write boundary](internal/app/app.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:1681) admits direct reports only from the request's addressee and refuses them while that reporter has a live effective promise on the request; otherwise the report closes the promise it cites. The [fold's requester lookup](internal/workroom/fold.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:2362) uses the admitted claim's originating request for either shape. The attached [current evidence and focused test results](direct-report-docs-evidence.json) records actual application and fold tests, exact source locations, and incorporated byte-equal live artifact bases. It distinguishes application submission tests from fold fixtures. No runtime defect or new authority is alleged.

Make the report-basis guidance internally consistent and explicit about the two existing paths. State who may report, when the live promise must be used, and how the originating requester accepts a non-merge report on either path. Correct the adjacent artifact paragraph if needed to avoid implying that direct assigned implementation is impossible; retain independent exact-head review and sealed-merge closure, with no extra implementation ratification. Never suggest withdrawing a live promise merely to bypass it. Keep the request's outcome/landing obligation and all identity, reserved-field, staleness, exact-commit and review rules intact. Use short linked explanations instead of duplicating the whole lifecycle in both pages.

Scope is docs/reference/gs/state.md and docs/reference/mcp/ratify.md, plus only a directly necessary link/provenance correction. Reconcile with then-current source before editing. #21365 owns the record-guide admission/fold wording, #21309 owns event identifiers, and #20305 owns AGENTS/SKILL editorial work; do not duplicate them. This follows up actual prose gaps in the #3029 migration cohort. It neither reopens completed comma retirement nor claims that all old migration conditions were met. No runtime, schema, workflow-state, authority, API, service, dependency or broad documentation rewrite is commissioned.

Use request/direct-report-reference-clarity. Verify the walkthroughs against real current behavior: no-promise addressee reports successfully; a stranger is refused; an existing live promise must be closed through itself; the originating requester accepts the direct non-merge report; direct implementation still proceeds through artifact/review/sealed merge. Use the named existing focused tests and appropriate existing documentation gates (make docs), then the repository-required validation at the final head. Do not add tests that mirror wording. Publish descriptive provenance on current behavior artifacts at each exact changed path, obtain independent Architecture/Security/Simplification review at the exact head, ratify approval, seal/push main and the workroom ref, verify CI, and remove the owned worktree and branch. Confirm availability and that no current assignment already owns these paragraphs before starting; retain this commission through ordinary inherited staleness, rechecking its conditions against current bases.

body.conditions: Make gs state and MCP ratify completion guidance match the two existing report shapes, preserving live-promise, performer, requester, review and landing rules; source-backed walkthroughs, documentation gates, independent review, seal/push/CI/cleanup. No runtime or policy change.
body.head: 3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b

Claude: correct two misleading glossary definitions and the related detach instruction. Queue after #21366; preserve current work and all earlier queue positions.

The [Attach definition](docs/reference/glossary.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:43) still says a non-forcing sequence fetch rule is installed. The [actual command](cmd/gs/main.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:3104) installs a forcing observation rule under refs/remotes/<name>/seq/*, removes both old direct mappings, and imports only after verification. The [current attach reference](docs/reference/gs/attach.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:63) already explains the distinction. Update the glossary with a short accurate definition and link to that reference.

The [Stale definition](docs/reference/glossary.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:135) implies any retired artifact ancestor is sufficient for describes_superseded_world. The [fold](internal/workroom/fold.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:2550) marks a direct retired-artifact edge, then propagates that narrower flag only through artifact-to-artifact provenance. A reasoning hop stops it even when ordinary staleness continues. Correct this entry without turning the glossary into another copy of the full merge rules; link to the existing detailed account and preserve governed terminal/exempt behavior. Do not say the initial direct dependent must itself be an artifact.

Align the [Leaving instruction](docs/how-to/publish-and-audit.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:129) with the exact generated tracking rule, preserving unrelated fetch mappings and making clear that deleting local Gitseq metadata discards rollback memory. This is instructional text only: do not remove live configuration, refs, checkpoints or custody. The [focused evidence](glossary-evidence.json) records passing actual disposable attach-command tests and fold fixtures, with their distinct limits, current-source comparisons and every selected live basis.

Scope: docs/reference/glossary.md and the necessary Leaving paragraph in docs/how-to/publish-and-audit.md, plus directly necessary links and descriptive provenance. Reconcile with then-current source. Preserve runtime, schemas, authority, state transitions, forced-push prohibition and verified import semantics. #21309 owns identifier guidance; #21365 record/admission wording; #21366 direct reports; #20305 AGENTS/SKILL. Do not duplicate those assignments, broaden to every glossary term, or reopen completed attachment/runtime work. This is another concrete prose gap from the partial #3029 migration audit; it does not certify all its original conditions. The unincorporated byte-equal glossary candidate 2cb7117f remains a separate live artifact; preserve it and let normal merge planning classify candidates rather than cleaning it up ad hoc.

Use request/glossary-behavior-clarity. Answer with a promise/queue or a specific viability reason; confirm availability and reconcile existing ownership before starting. Retain ordinary inherited staleness rather than deleting provenance to make the row fresh. Verify both edge cases using the named focused tests and existing documentation gates, including links and the publish/audit walkthrough; no wording-mirror tests. Publish exact changed paths on current behavior bases, obtain independent exact-head Architecture/Security/Simplification review, ratify approval, seal/push main and workroom refs, check CI and remove the owned worktree/branch. Final delivery is the corrected documentation, not merely another review note.

body.conditions: Correct Attach and Stale glossary definitions plus the related Leaving instruction against current behavior; preserve all runtime/authority rules, use verified links and focused existing tests, then independent review/seal/push/CI/cleanup. No live configuration or ref changes.
body.head: 3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b

Claude: make gs batch use the same explicit identity selection as gs state. Queue after #21367, preserving active #21309 and every earlier commitment.

The [batch reference](docs/reference/gs/batch.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:22) allows --as or GITSEQ_ACTOR, but [batchCommand](cmd/gs/main.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:1822) refuses whenever --as is absent and continues to pass the raw flag to signing. [ResolveActor](internal/residentclient/client.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:44) already owns the intended rule: explicit flag, otherwise the nonblank environment identity, otherwise refusal. A fresh current-main binary and disposable signed workroom reproduce this: gs state with GITSEQ_ACTOR=probe-b appends as probe-b; the equivalent batch refuses before appending; explicit --as probe-a overrides the environment and signs as probe-a. Missing and unknown environment cases also append nothing, although the latter currently fails before key resolution. [Proof and limits](batch-signing-evidence.json) include exact heads, actor checks and before/after sequence refs.

Use the existing shared resolver once at the batch boundary and pass its resolved actor consistently to key lookup, preflight, signing and execution. Preserve explicit-flag precedence, trimmed environment selection, no implicit/default actor, unavailable-key refusal before append, one signer per chain, existing role/admission checks, per-act idempotency and typed batch results. Test real batch execution with environment-only identity, conflicting explicit/environment identities, missing or blank identity, and an unavailable environment identity; verify actual signed actors and no append on refusal. Reuse the current batch fixtures and add a focused regression that fails when environment resolution is removed; do not replace this with a helper-only or documentation-text test.

Also correct this page's [opening cost claim](docs/reference/gs/batch.md@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:12). It says every other durable command verifies the whole log each time, while the [current snapshot path](internal/app/app.go@3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b:2508) distinguishes cache, signed checkpoint/tail and cold audit. The named checkpoint test passed on this head. Explain the actual benefit of one opened workspace and ordered label/resumption handling, distinguish client preparation from resident sequencing, and avoid claiming a full audit or constant-time path without evidence. No cache, transport or performance redesign is needed.

Use request/batch-signing-identity. Reconcile with then-current main and #21309's batch-reference changes before starting; its examined private67aca15f still has this gap. Limit source changes to routing batch through the existing identity contract, its meaningful tests and truthful batch documentation/provenance. This does not revive the broader reverted instance-identity work: Hugh's #14665 disposition of #14147 remains intact, including all decided-against behavior. No new keys, shared-session refusal, actor lifecycle policy, security posture, live workroom operation or #8162 work is commissioned.

Answer with a promise/queue or explicit viability reason. Current selected source bases are live and byte-equal to incorporated main; keep ordinary staleness visible and recheck before acting. Preserve completed #21335 proper-prefix recovery controls. Run focused batch/identity tests and existing documentation gates, then required repository checks; obtain independent exact-head Architecture, Security and Simplification review, updating architecture only if a contract actually changes. Publish each changed path on its behavior bases, ratify approval, seal/push main and workroom refs, verify CI and remove the owned worktree/branch. Completion requires working environment-only batch signing, not merely deleting its documented support.

body.conditions: Route gs batch through existing flag/environment actor resolution with actual signed-actor and no-append regression coverage; correct its unconditional full-audit claim, preserve all batch/admission behavior and prior identity dispositions; independent review/seal/push/CI/cleanup.
body.head: 3ecb8b77d55cfe8ccb1d634649788a4ab629577b
